title: Reward Model Overoptimization Under Compute Constraints: When Does It Start?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear chain: identifying the training step at which overoptimization begins enables early stopping heuristics. Directly actionable for small-scale safety researchers running RL fine-tuning.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running PPO fine-tuning of a 7B model requires an RLHF pipeline (e.g., TRL), which is complex setup for beginners. Tracking every 100 steps across three reward models multiplies the compute requirement. Medium compute may be borderline.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single variable (training step) tracked against two metrics (reward score, alignment probe). The three reward models add scope but the experimental structure is clear. Feasible if limited to one reward model.
